Leveraging the SPDK framework (Intel, 2016) with 8 PCIe lanes (4 lanes per SSD), this setup achieves a peak read throughput [...] Empirical Potential Analysis and FPGA Prototyping: We validate ITME by evaluating its performance potential using production-grade SK hynix CMM (SK hynix, 2024) and Gen5 NVMe SSDs (KIOXIA, 2024), while further demonstrating functional feasibility through an FPGA-based hardware prototype. ## 2. Background and Motivation [...] ITME serves as a high-performance memory backend that integrates seamlessly with established tiering mechanisms. Furthermore, its internal hardware-level prefetching complements various scheduling policies, effectively hiding access latency by overlapping data movement with ongoing computation. This synergy allows ITME to maximize KV cache reuse and system efficiency within any established inference hierarchy.

Key-value cache is one of the most important memory challenges in large-language-model inference. During autoregressive generation, transformer models store key and value tensors from previous tokens. This avoids recomputing attention over the entire context. As context windows become longer, KV cache memory requirements grow significantly. [...] This tiered approach can make enterprise AI more practical. It reduces the need to keep everything in expensive memory and reduces the latency penalty of retrieving everything from slower storage.

## 10. KV Cache, Long Context, and Memory Expansion [...] HBM is the correct place for the most active KV cache data. However, not all session history is equally active. Older cache blocks or less frequently accessed context may be candidates for tiering. DRAM and HBF can support overflow or warm-cache strategies if software can manage migration intelligently.
